Four schemes

Same palette, same rules, different story about what this ship used to be.

Scheme 1 of 4

Service Rings

Rust is the connective tissue and it reaches everywhere. Every heavy machine stands on an iron-plate island edged in iron grate; the landing pads are plate with a worn-yellow lip. Reads as one system somebody maintained bay by bay for a very long time.

Reads asSomebody maintained this, bay by bay, for centuries.

  • metal plating (iron)1301

  • scaffold tile117

Cost to layLowest risk. The bays fall out of the machine footprints, so it survives you moving a machine later.

Scheme 2 of 4

Hazard Lanes

The same bays, plus worn-yellow grate lanes running the full spine and both legs, and yellow at every leg mouth and pad lip. Reads as a working plant whose crew had marked routes and somewhere to be.

Reads asThis was a plant with a shift pattern and marked routes.

Cost to laySame bays plus 453 lane cells. The lanes are hand-placed, so they break if the legs are re-cut.

Scheme 3 of 4

Cargo Decks

Big blocks instead of islands: the whole lower ship - legs and pads - is dock plating, and the spine is divoted rust, the one thing used nowhere else. Reads as a hauler whose spine was the important part.

Reads asThis was a hauler, and the spine was the part that mattered.

Scheme 4 of 4

Stratified Hull

Rust worn through to bare ancient hull in patches across the ring and spine; the legs are hull and never had rust. Reads as older than its own fittings - the rust is a later layer over something that outlasted it.

Reads asThe rust is a later layer. Something under it outlasted the crew.

Can the greys be pushed to ancient hull?

Yes. RimWorld’s 1.6 colour grid tints any floor — and it multiplies, so it can only darken.

  • no tint

    126 118 103

  • Structure_GrayLight

    120 120 120

    neutral, same lightness

  • Structure_Marble

    95 97 95

    neutral, a shade under

  • Structure_Granite

    73 66 68

    the match

  • ancient hull tile

    71 71 71

    the target

Structure_Granite lands it. Scaffold tile reads 126 118 103 raw — warm, sandy, the lightest thing on the ship. Tinted Granite it reads 73 66 68 against ancient hull’s 71 71 71. Same lightness, a hair warmer. Structure_Marble is the softer version if the engine room should still be the brightest room aboard.

The catch is worth knowing before you rely on it: the tint is a multiply, so every ColorDef darkens and none can lighten. A floor can always be pushed toward oxide and toward hull. Nothing can be pushed back up. Choose the lightest tile you might want, then tint down.

How to pick

Three questions decide it. The rest is paint.

Islands or blocks?

Service Rings and Hazard Lanes read the ship as bays in a field of rust. Cargo Decks reads it as two big zones with a spine. Islands carry more information; blocks carry more weight.

How loud is the yellow?

Service Rings keeps it to 122 cells — lips and thresholds only. Hazard Lanes spends 453 on marked routes. Yellow is the only thing on this ship a player will follow with their eyes.

Is the ship old, or is it older than itself?

Three schemes say a thousand years of maintenance. Stratified Hull says the rust is a recent layer over something that was already ancient — and the legs never got the upgrade.

Machinery is drawn as a translucent slab so the floor under it still reads. Walls are grey; the three doors are gold.
